passages.provision_quote: Allows the fiscal body of Monroe County to adopt an ordinance to impose an additional local income tax rate to fund one or more county transit projects.
passages.note: House cosponsorship of a bill enabling a county transit income tax shows support for transit investment but sets nothing against road capacity, so it does not separate rung 1 from rung 2.
Concern that replacing gas-tax revenue for road repairs could crowd out non-transportation priorities speaks to the budget as a whole, not to the split between roads and other modes.
The forum transcript does not address transportation investment.

rows.reasoning: Pierce cosponsored SB 128 (2016), which "Allows the fiscal body of Monroe County to adopt an ordinance to impose an additional local income tax rate to fund one or more county transit projects"; this shows support for transit investment but does not put it "over new road capacity" (rung 1) or set an equal split (rung 2). No other passage speaks to the roads-versus-other-modes split.

quotes.text: I am concerned that if the Iran war and gas tax suspension continue with no end in sight, the need to replace lost revenue for road repairs could crowd out funding desperately needed for priorities like schools, health care , child care, and affordable housing
